analysis.session_summary: The dollar rejected early weakness and led the board after US core CPI printed 0.3% versus 0.2%, adding 0.457% to the USD basket. EUR and GBP led early but gave back 73% and 98% of those gains respectively, closing as the weakest majors. Central-bank remarks from Lagarde, Bailey and Macklem all scored muted or unscored, leaving the CPI release as the only tradable impulse. The tape shows risk-sensitive currencies failed to hold early gains while USD/CHF and USD/MXN saw pronounced repricing.

themes.theme: US core CPI triggers broad dollar repricing
themes.evidence: Core CPI m/m +3 more actual 0.3% vs forecast 0.2% produced USD own-currency impulse +0.457%; USD/CHF +0.62%, USD/JPY +0.217%, EUR/USD -0.59%, DXY +0.534%.

themes.theme: Early high-beta and European FX gains rejected
themes.evidence: EUR led +0.06% then gave back 73%; GBP led +0.09% then gave back 98%; AUD led +0.37% then gave back 62%; NZD led +0.12% then gave back 90%.
Lagarde's remarks scored muted 0.012% and unscored -0.046%; Bailey basket moved 0.012%; Macklem basket moved -0.015%, all inside the noise floor.

currency_drivers.USD: US core CPI beat at 0.3% vs 0.2% added 0.457%, reversing early selling into broad demand.
currency_drivers.EUR: ECB Lagarde's remarks scored unscored or muted; EUR led +0.06% then gave back 73%.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own releases; closed at its best (+0.209%) with no direct catalyst.
currency_drivers.GBP: BOE Bailey's speech was muted; GBP led +0.09% then gave back 98% to close weakest.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own releases; led +0.37% then gave back 62%, still positive for the day.
currency_drivers.CAD: BOC Macklem's speech was muted; closed at its best (+0.086%) with no tradable impulse.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own releases; led +0.07% then gave back 94% to close lower.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own releases; led +0.12% then gave back 90% to close near lows.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: The pair first rose 19.0 pips with no clear catalyst, then fell 87.1 pips in a leg where US CPI accounted for 68% of the move.

polarity_reads.read: Normal beat polarity (USD +0.457%) shows positioning was not fighting USD strength; USD/CHF sigma 14.09 indicates a short-dollar squeeze.
Scored muted at 0.012% and later unscored at -0.046%, indicating no new information to reprice EUR, so positioning was flat.
Muted 0.012% basket move inside noise means Bailey added nothing; GBP weakness was USD-driven, not BOE-driven.
Muted -0.015% basket move inside noise argues no CAD-specific positioning was triggered.

scenarios.name: USD inflation repricing extends
scenarios.thesis: The CPI beat reinforces higher-for-longer USD; firm US PPI/retail sales extend dollar gains while commodity FX stabilizes but lags.
triggers: US Core Retail Sales m/m above 0.6%
scenarios.invalidation: US data miss or risk sentiment flips sharply risk-on

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD already fell 66.0 pips today; another USD-positive surprise can match that downside.
USD/JPY rose 34.5 pips on CPI; extension would target the 158.74 close plus further yen underperformance.

scenarios.name: Post-CPI consolidation
scenarios.thesis: Market digests the USD spike; majors hold ranges near current levels as participants reduce positions ahead of the next US data block.
triggers: US data prints close to consensus
Equities stabilize and VIX fades from 17.26
scenarios.invalidation: Break of EUR/USD 1.11234 or USD/JPY 158.742 on strong follow-through

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD range today was 98.1 pips; consolidation argues for staying inside that band.
USD/CHF range was 77.9 pips, and a range scenario respects the 0.83834 close.

scenarios.name: USD reversal on soft US data
scenarios.thesis: If PPI/retail sales miss, the CPI-driven USD bid unwinds and crowded long-USD positioning from the CPI reaction violently reverses.
triggers: US Core Retail Sales m/m below 0.6%
scenarios.invalidation: US core CPI effects dominate and data beats

pair_paths.rationale: A reversal of today's 66.0-pip EUR/USD decline would see the pair revisit the pre-CPI starting point.
GBP/USD was down 89.0 pips; a USD unwind could retrace that move.

risks.risk: USD short-squeeze extends on US data
risks.why_it_matters: Normal CPI beat drove USD/CHF sigma 14.09 and DXY +0.534%, leaving crowded short-dollar trades vulnerable.
EUR and GBP gave back early gains and closed at the bottom of their ranges, making them vulnerable to soft GDP/retail sales.
VIX/USD rose 2.983% to 17.26, signaling fragile equities; high-beta FX may underperform.
